answer_1.quote: Alignment of LLMs to human preferences is important for their general applicability. Constrained decoding in large language models (LLMs) is an effective method as a post-training step to align LLM generations to human preferences such as harmless text generation, faithful summarization, formatted generation, flow adhering planning, among other use cases.
answer_1.outputs: generated text sequences under lexical and semantic constraints

answer_2.quote: For CommonGen, we report two constraint satisfaction metrics -(1) % Soft Constraint Satisfaction: measures the overall percentage of constraints that are satisfied across all data points, (2) % Hard Constraint Satisfaction: measures the percentage of data points where all required concepts are included. For HTG, we measure the percentage of generations that are harmless.

answer_3.quote: For evaluating if a generated response is harmless, we use an off-the-shelf LLM, Llama-Guard-3-8B (Llama Team, 2024), which is fine-tuned for content safety classification task to assess the safety of the generated text.

answer_4.quote: We use Amazon SageMaker Ground Truth for the evaluation, where the annotators are presented with the same prompt as Llama-Guard (as shown in Figure ) along with some positive and negative examples and are instructed to mark the Assistant response as safe or unsafe.
answer_4.guideline: annotators are instructed to mark the Assistant response as safe or unsafe based on the prompt and provided examples
